title: MIGER: Integrating Multi-Instance GPU and Multi-Process Service for Deep Learning Clusters
authors: Bowen Zhang and Shuxin Li and Zhuozhao Li
mechanism: MIG partitions with per-partition MPS online/offline co-location, local partition planner and fragmentation control
environment: Two servers, each 2 Intel Xeon Gold 5320 CPUs and 4 A100 80GB GPUs; CUDA 12.0; per-partition MPS daemons and DCGM. OS/driver not yet extracted.
workload: Table 3 inference/training models, including ResNet50, MobileNet, BERT and U-net. 150 jobs of 30 min to 2 h; Poisson arrival parameter 60 s. Local MPS/MIG examples separated from eight-GPU testbed and 128-GPU simulation.
comparator: MuxFlow (MPS) and modified MISO (MIG); MISO adapted to preserve online jobs during reconfiguration.
finding: Section 3.1/Fig. 2 directly compares local MPS 57/29/14 percent and MIG 4g/2g/1g allocations. Section 5.2/Fig. 8 reports testbed mean JCT 46.6% below MuxFlow and 36% below MISO; these are job/cluster outcomes, not inference p99 gains. Fig. 9 notes slower small jobs under MIGER.
limitation: Includes mixed training/inference and multi-GPU optimization; retain only explicitly local sharing and inference-QoS evidence for assigned comparison. title: SPLIT: QoS-Aware DNN Inference on Shared GPU via Evenly-Sized Model Splitting
authors: Diaohan Luo and Tian Yu and Yuewen Wu and Heng Wu and Tao Wang and Wenbo Zhang
mechanism: SPLIT: genetic offline model-block splitting with token-based greedy temporal preemption
environment: Jetson Nano; Ubuntu 18.04; ONNX Runtime 1.12.1. CUDA/driver versions not yet extracted.
workload: YOLOv2, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, VGG19, GPT-2; 1000 requests per scenario, Poisson average intervals 160 to 110 ms across six scenarios; latency target alpha times isolated execution time, alpha 2-20.
comparator: Clockwork-like sequential policy, PREMA-like preemption and Runtime-aware multi-stream approach (RT-A); these adapted baselines differ in concurrency.
finding: Section 5.5 reports violation rate below 10% beyond alpha=4 versus 26% under RT-A in the discussed comparison. For short requests, jitter reductions versus Clockwork/PREMA/RT-A are 55.3/46.8/68.9% at low load and 56.0/50.3/69.3% at high load. Jitter is block-execution standard deviation, not p99 latency. Section 6 reports split overhead and static-graph limits.
limitation: One edge GPU and synthetic Poisson load; not a server-class GPU generalization. Temporal predictability sacrifices spatial parallelism; long-request stability can worsen. Table 3 split overhead and RNN limits qualify short-request improvements.
